video_title: Lakers Relying Too Much On Luka? + Concern For Ant Edwards Injury? & Players Who Deserve More Shine

quotes.speaker: Ben Golliver
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic's heavy workload and lack of scoring support
quotes.excerpt: it just feels like a one-man show with Luka and the burden, the toll of creating shots
quotes.quote: The vibes in general in LA have been really good. There was a one-game adjustment period to no LeBron. Opening night was really weird, it felt like there was a hole, but as the win streak has gone along, the crowds have been really strong. They went in excited, expecting Luka to put up 50 against one of the worst teams in the league. Second night of a back-to-back, no Austin Reaves, it just didn't go that way. As it was getting away from them down the stretch, there were definitely some groans and grumbles about, hey, who else is scoring here? It just feels like a one-man show with Luka and the burden, the toll of creating so many shots for the Lakers, especially when Austin isn't out there, is weighing a little bit on Luka already.
quotes.social_post: Luka Doncic is carrying a massive load for the Lakers. With Austin Reaves out, the reliance on Luka as a one-man show is becoming a real concern for the team's sustainability.

quotes.speaker: Ben Golliver
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic's historic usage rate and sustainability concerns
quotes.excerpt: There's never been a player with a usage above 35 ever to win a championship
quotes.quote: This is the highest usage rate he's ever had in his career, obviously the highest scoring average he's ever had in his career. He's always been a high-usage, high-scoring player, going back to the Mavericks days. This is the purest form of Luka, peak Luka. But the question always becomes about sustainability, diminishing returns. Can you keep this up? Is it the healthiest way to play? Hanging over this is, there's never been a player with a usage above 35 ever to win a championship. Usually, they're down in the low 30s, and Luka's above 40 right now. Usually, that's a red flag when people are looking at this.
quotes.social_post: Luka Doncic is operating at a 40 percent usage rate, well above the historical threshold for championship teams. The question remains if this level of play is sustainable for a deep playoff run.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic's need for a lob threat and secondary creator
quotes.excerpt: The most important thing that Luka needs, there's two critical things that Luka has to have
quotes.quote: There are a lot of similarities between that Mavericks team and this Lakers team. The most important thing that Luka needs, there's two critical things that Luka has to have. One, a legitimate lob threat as a big, and then two, a co-star who is comfortable playing off the ball and can also create with the ball in his hands. With the Mavericks, it was the Gafford-Lively tag team and then obviously Kyrie. With the Lakers, it's Kessler, who I think Kessler is going to really need to continue getting better as a pick-and-roll partner. Pick first and then roll hard, partner. And then obviously Austin Reaves being healthy is essential.
quotes.social_post: For Luka Doncic to thrive, he needs a legitimate lob threat and a co-star who can create off the ball. The Lakers are still searching for that consistent pick-and-roll chemistry.

quotes.speaker: Ben Golliver
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic's usage rate and time of possession
quotes.quote: Before the game, he said, I don't believe in usage rate. He was essentially saying as a staff, they put more emphasis on time of possession. So the idea is, it goes back to what I was saying with Harden. If Harden has to dribble for 20 seconds before he shoots, that's going to have this accumulation factor. You're more likely to get tired by the end of the game or by the end of the season. With Luka, they're trying to get him off the ball more, and then in turn, even though he's shooting a ton, drawing a lot of free throws like we said, maybe it's quicker decisions so that he doesn't have to dominate the ball and do that all game long. It is interesting because Luka is number one by a mile in usage rate, but he's only ranked fourth by time of possession.
quotes.social_post: Luka Doncic leads the league in usage rate but ranks fourth in time of possession. The coaching staff is pushing for quicker decisions to reduce the physical toll on him over the course of the season.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Edwards' knee surgery and recovery timeline
quotes.excerpt: I'm just trying to get strength back in my leg, I think that's the most difficult part
quotes.quote: Anthony Edwards gave an interview for the first time, I believe, since he had knee surgery a couple of weeks ago. I'm going to read these quotes. He said, quote, I'm the type of guy, I never wanted to have surgery. Like I thought it would just go away. In the offseason, it was actually good. Like we were managing it pretty good, treating it, and it wasn't as swollen, and then like soon the season kicked off, I don't know what happened. It just flared back up like really bad, and then I was like, man, it's time. He was then asked if he estimated whether it would be weeks or months, and he tempered expectations by saying that. He talked about the decision to have the surgery. He said, quote, it needed to be done in order for me to be able to play without any pain for the next couple of years. But who knows? Maybe in a couple of years, I might have to get something else. But hopefully not. I think I'll be pretty good.
quotes.social_post: Anthony Edwards opens up about his recent knee surgery, admitting he tried to manage the pain before it flared up. He hopes this procedure allows him to play pain-free for years to come.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Edwards' recovery and the Timberwolves' depth
quotes.excerpt: There's no reason whatsoever for Ant to rush back. He's not going to be award eligible
quotes.quote: Ant did not get a medical degree during his semester and a half at Georgia. But look, in all seriousness, take your time. There's no reason whatsoever for Ant to rush back. He's not going to be award eligible, and he doesn't have to like rush to grab his cape out of the closet and save the Timberwolves because they're having a phenomenal season despite his absence. They're 11 and 4 and have the second-best point differential in the league. So obviously, Ant wants to play basketball, he wants to be part of this, he wants to continue to build chemistry, especially with Mike Conley. But the most important thing is he's back, he's healthy, and that they're going to have him in a rhythm and fresh rolling into the playoffs because they're going to be a playoff team.
quotes.social_post: There is no reason for Anthony Edwards to rush back from surgery. The Timberwolves are playing at a high level and the priority is having him healthy and in rhythm for the playoffs.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Rookies with high minutes and the history of the draft
quotes.excerpt: Shane Battier, wow. Who was the coach? Was that Hubie Brown?
quotes.quote: I wanted to know the last few guys who averaged over 38 minutes a game as rookies. And Jackson looked it up for us. So, Shane Battier. Wow. Who was the coach? Was that Hubie Brown? Was he the coach in Memphis? Probably. Battier averaged 39. He averaged 40 minutes a game as a rookie. Couldn't take him off the court. LeBron averaged 39 and a half, but I'm going to tell you the second half of that year, they actually won some games and were trying to like get back into the playoff race. I bet he averaged well over. There were games at the end of the season where Paul Silas didn't take him off the court. Damian Lillard averaged 39, 38.6. Sydney Lowe, by the way, Jackson says. OJ Mayo, 38 minutes. Only players since 2000 to average over 38 minutes a game that A-Cuff, he's not quite there, he's just underneath, he's sniffing it.
quotes.social_post: A look back at rookie minutes: only a handful of players since 2000 have averaged over 38 minutes per game, including LeBron James and Damian Lillard. It is a rare and heavy workload for a first-year player.

quotes.speaker: Ben Golliver
quotes.summary_phrase: 76ers' success in clutch games and sustainability
quotes.excerpt: I kind of believe in Maxey as a closer though, he inspires a lot of confidence
quotes.quote: I should sell high on the 76ers clutch. I kind of believe in Maxey as a closer though. He inspires a lot of confidence.
quotes.social_post: Tyrese Maxey is proving to be a reliable closer for the 76ers. His ability to perform in the clutch is starting to inspire real confidence in Philadelphia.

quotes.speaker: Ben Golliver
quotes.summary_phrase: Dejounte Murray trade rumors and the Pelicans' interest
quotes.excerpt: There's been a lot of Dejounte Murray for Jaylen Brown smoke. That smoke is not coming from Phoenix
quotes.quote: He's been in the trade rumor mill. There's been a lot of Dejounte Murray for Jaylen Brown smoke. What I can tell you is that smoke is not coming from Phoenix. It is certainly not something that the Suns are excited about. And if that sort of a trade is going to materialize, the value is not going to be Dejounte Murray. The value is going to be whatever pick that the Pelicans would be able to, would be willing to put in that deal. And if you're the Pelicans, you absolutely shouldn't even be considering putting a kind of pick in a deal like that. That would be a value.
quotes.social_post: The Dejounte Murray trade rumors are heating up, but the Suns do not appear to be the driving force. Any deal involving the Pelicans would likely hinge on draft capital rather than Murray himself.

quotes.speaker: Ben Golliver
quotes.summary_phrase: The Suns' depth and the trade market for point guards
quotes.excerpt: The Suns don't see the point guard situation as something that they have an urgent need to upgrade
quotes.quote: I've been told that the Suns don't see the point guard situation as something that they have an urgent need to upgrade. And frankly, the Kings very much valued Nick Collison. And the other thing I'll say on that is I'm not sure Dejounte Murray is upgrading anything.
quotes.social_post: The Suns do not view their point guard situation as an urgent need for an upgrade. There is skepticism around the league regarding whether Dejounte Murray would actually move the needle for them.

quotes.speaker: Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jackson's relentless trash talking on the court
quotes.excerpt: I talk trash relentlessly at all times.

text_blocks.speaker: Jackson
text_blocks.text: I talk trash relentlessly at all times. What I've done last has nothing to do with that. It's just if we're leading on the scoreboard, then I'm feeling good about things. Sometimes I talk trash to my own teammates. Jaren Jackson Jr. are one of our producers on NBA Today. Have I ever told you this story?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Jaren is very well respected behind the scenes, but Jaren is known for not keeping anything in the bag. He would be the worst poker player in the history of the sport. He just tells everybody everything.

quotes.social_post: Jackson admits he is a relentless trash talker on the court, even against his own teammates. Apparently, Jaren Jackson Jr. is the same way, making him the worst poker player in the sport.

quotes.speaker: Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaren Jackson Jr.'s D3 college basketball background
quotes.excerpt: He also was a D3 point guard. Apparently he led the country in free throw shooting.
quotes.quote: He also was a D3 point guard. Apparently he led the country in free throw shooting and then they put him on the air and he bricks one. He pulled a Bam Adebayo.
quotes.social_post: Jaren Jackson Jr. has a D3 basketball background, but even he is not immune to the occasional airball. He pulled a classic Bam Adebayo moment on the court.

quotes.speaker: Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jackson's experience in a Warriors pickup tournament
quotes.excerpt: We got the Warriors old facility in Oakland and we have a pickup run.
quotes.quote: We got the Warriors old facility in Oakland and we have a pickup run. It was Dave's one thing that he insisted on. We got to play basically like a pickup tournament. I was on Jaren's team. I had a lot of screen assists for Jaren that day. We were doing pretty well and Dave didn't do so well that day. So at the end, he joins our team. He wanted to go out on top. Anyways, it gets to game point and we've got a comfortable lead. So like dude, the groom's got to get the rock. The groom's got to hit the walk-off shot. Jaren takes like an 18-foot off-dribble baseline fadeaway and I mean it's like the worst awareness I've ever seen from a point guard in my life. Thank God he bricked it and I did set a solid screen assist, got Jaren open look, he knocked it down. We mob him and then he's off to wedded bliss afterwards. But Jaren almost messed up the entire wedding with his just selfish gunning. It was embarrassing.
quotes.social_post: Jaren Jackson Jr. almost ruined his own wedding pickup game with some questionable shot selection. Nothing like a selfish baseline fadeaway to test the nerves before the big day.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The wedding ring mishap during the ceremony
quotes.excerpt: When it came time to present the rings, his best man, his brother, didn't have them.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Jackson, we don't talk about pickup, we talk about the NBA. It was an old NBA facility. Forget about the best man speech, it's the best man screen, I guess. You know what? I can confirm his trash talking. Jackson's been on the wrong end of a lot of it. McMenamin would prefer a best man screen to a best man speech.

text_blocks.speaker: Jackson
text_blocks.text: There was a pretty good, I don't know if he was best man, but one of our old colleagues had a pretty good speech.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: I will say, we thought it was some sort of shtick, but it was true. When it came time to present the rings, his best man, his brother, didn't have them. Didn't have them and like we thought, you know, we thought it was just like a bad joke. Nope. He didn't have them. They had to go into the audience and people had to pull rings off their fingers to produce rings to act as stand-in rings.

text_blocks.speaker: Jackson
text_blocks.text: All's well that ends well. They found them.

quotes.social_post: Talk about a wedding disaster. The best man forgot the rings, forcing guests to pull jewelry off their own fingers to serve as stand-ins. Thankfully, they eventually found the real ones.
